walkthroughs.body_html:
Operations Management — a core area of GCSE Business Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Operations Management brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Operations Management.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What three Ps are added to make the extended marketing mix (7Ps)?
options: People (staff/service quality), Process (how the service is delivered), and Physical Evidence (tangible cues — uniforms, packaging, branding) — added to make the 4Ps relevant to services marketing.
Porter's Five Forces are five physical security measures for a factory.
The 7Ps include Profit, Planning and Performance.
The 7Ps are just the 4Ps repeated with different words.
Porter's Five Forces are five business strategies a firm should choose between.
The 7Ps include Profit, Planning and Performance.

Competitive rivalry, threat of new entrants, threat of substitutes, bargaining power of suppliers, bargaining power of buyers — together determining industry attractiveness and potential profitability.

mcqs.q: What are Porter's two main generic strategies for competitive advantage?
options: Porter's Five Forces are five physical security measures for a factory.
Porter's strategies are about marketing channels.
Porter says businesses should pursue both low cost and differentiation at once.
Cost leadership (being the lowest-cost producer) and differentiation (offering unique value customers will pay more for) — Porter argues firms should choose one or the other.
